description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary findings.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing the thorax. The image reveals bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, more prominent in the upper lung zones. There are no visible pleural effusions or pneumothorax. The clavicles and ribs appear intact, and there are no obvious skeletal abnormalities. The radiograph also shows the presence of medical devices, likely ECG leads, on the chest wall.
visible_findings: more prominent findings in upper lung zones
no visible pleural effusions or pneumothorax
presence of medical devices on chest wall

description.short_caption: Axial CT scan of the head and neck.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image shows a cross-sectional view of the head and neck region. The scan highlights soft tissue structures, bony anatomy, and air-filled spaces. There is no visible contrast enhancement, suggesting a non-contrast study. The image appears to be focused on the upper cervical region, with clear visualization of the vertebrae, airway, and surrounding soft tissues.
visible_findings: axial view of head and neck
soft tissue structures surrounding the airway
reveal_triggers: axial CT of head and neck

description.short_caption: Ultrasound with Doppler showing a vascular structure with flow characteristics.
description.detailed_description: This is a Doppler ultrasound image showing a longitudinal view of a vascular structure, likely a vein, with blue and red color signals indicating blood flow direction and velocity. The vessel appears patent, and the surrounding soft tissue is visible. The Doppler overlay suggests active flow within the vessel, with no obvious signs of obstruction or thrombosis.
visible_findings: blue and red Doppler signals indicating blood flow

Case_01012/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Doppler study of right internal jugular vein.

description.short_caption: Doppler ultrasound of the right internal jugular vein showing blood flow.
description.detailed_description: This is a Doppler ultrasound image of the right internal jugular vein. The vessel is visualized in a longitudinal plane, with color Doppler overlay indicating blood flow. Blue and red color signals represent flow direction relative to the transducer, consistent with venous blood flow. The surrounding soft tissue appears hypoechoic to hyperechoic. The scale on the right indicates flow velocity in cm/s.
visible_findings: color Doppler overlay showing blood flow
blue and red signals indicating flow direction
